comparison: Perfect alignment on xenograft heterogeneity claims (C29-C36). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative metrics and statistical comparisons, while peer reviewers note the solid experimental design across model systems without specific concerns about xenograft data.

Perfect alignment on immunohistochemistry findings (C74-C75, C94-C95). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights this as a valuable negative result ruling out epithelial/mesenchymal markers as sources of heterogeneity. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of solid experimental characterization without challenge.

Strong alignment on patient sample heterogeneity data (C37-C48). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes adequate sample size (n=29) for descriptive statistics and documents the lack of correlation between bimodality and dispersion. Peer reviewers affirm the findings and note that 8 additional patients were added during revision, strengthening conclusions.

Strong alignment on cell line homogeneity claims (C20-C26). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of FLIM measurements and statistical analysis. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the solid experimental foundation without raising concerns.

Strong alignment on the core hierarchical heterogeneity finding (C1, C2, C58). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval synthesizes quantitative measurements across all model systems. All three peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as the study's merit, with the editor stating the evidence is 'solid.'

Alignment on technical capabilities and clinical potential (C88-C91, C97). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes resolution advantages and appropriately framed future possibilities. Peer reviewers affirm the value of the approach for quantifying metabolic heterogeneity and note it provides valuable results for deploying optical imaging techniques.

Perfect alignment on flavin detection limitation (C88). Both evaluations find this SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents the technical limitation with quantitative data. Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges the authors attempted to incorporate flavin fluorescence but could not find strong enough signal.

Partial alignment on clinical associations (C3, C51-C52, C54-C56). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to limited sample size and marginal p-values, noting need for validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting the associations while acknowledging limitations and noting that additional samples were added during revision.

Alignment on prognostic potential with acknowledged limitations (C5, C57, C93). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing limited sample size and need for validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED but acknowledge limitations, with Reviewer 2 noting 'maybe more patients should be involved in the future for reliable diagnosis and prognosis.'

Alignment on analytical findings (C50, C53). OpenEval rates the broader claim set UNCERTAIN due to sample size limitations. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED for the specific analytical findings without raising concerns, accepting the moderate ability to distinguish tumor stages.

Alignment on lack of correlation between bimodality and dispersion (C46-C48). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this demonstrates the metrics capture different aspects of heterogeneity. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the solid patient tumor heterogeneity data.

Minimal overlap on heterogeneity metrics (C4). OpenEval R6 focuses on lack of correlation between metrics as a specific finding (SUPPORTED). Peer R2 addresses broader clinical associations including C4 among other claims (SUPPORTED).

Minimal overlap on study value (C92). OpenEval R4 synthesizes comparative findings across model systems (SUPPORTED). Peer R10 addresses technical capabilities and study value including C92 among broader claims about the approach's uniqueness (SUPPORTED).
